calls.reason: The 89% figure matches The Information's annualised sample of 34 startups, but that sample leaves out listed companies and AI clouds. Nothing in the packet measures a realised industry-wide remainder against the $20B ceiling.

TrendForce confirms AI demand is squeezing memory supply, and Huang's ~$100B-per-GW estimate circulated in July 2026. But no comparable earlier cost figure or cost breakdown shows a doubling caused by memory.

OpenAI's total Q1 outlays come to about $9.4B ($5.7B revenue plus $3.7B burn). Epoch puts AI capex near $1T annualised and the two labs at only 15–20% of compute, so their compute spend can hardly be 70% of all AI industry revenue.

Filed RPO and backlog (Microsoft $627B, Amazon $364B, Google over $460B) total about $1.45T, so $448B would be about 31%, not 50%. Microsoft also reports 26% RPO growth excluding OpenAI, which contradicts the 'flat' claim and the idea that other demand is small.

This is a conditional forecast whose trigger has not happened. NVIDIA's August 2026 call describes record revenue, a supply-constrained outlook and rising hyperscaler capex, and no downturn sequence is documented.
The claim is hedged and covers all of 2026, which has not ended. Anthropic's S-1 gives $16.3B of first-half revenue for one company only, with no combined full-year revenue or compute-spend totals.
